predecessors.note: 'Liuvigild sent Hermenegild to the south to govern on his behalf' (Hermenegild page); the Liuvigild page: 'Baetica revolted under the leadership of Hermenegild'.

land.text: Baetica, whose rebellion under Hermenegild the Liuvigild page dates 579-584

successors.note: Seville fell to Liuvigild in 584; Hermenegild was executed on 13 April 585.

capitals.name: Seville (Hispalis)
capitals.note: 'Hermenegild fled to Seville and when it fell to a siege in 584, he went to Cordoba'.

correction.text: Baetica, whose rebellion under Hermenegild the Liuvigild page dates 579-584

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Baetica in revolt. The Liuvigild page says 'Baetica revolted under the leadership of Hermenegild' and that Liuvigild took Merida in 582 and Seville in 584; the pages do not draw a boundary, so Baetica is the reading and Merida (held by Bishop Masona, not the rebels) stays out.

region.text: Baetica, whose rebellion under Hermenegild the Liuvigild page dates 579-584

ledger.note: 580: Hermenegild, governor of the south, rebels against his father Liuvigild. 'He fell out with his father in 579, then revolted the following year'; the Liuvigild page dates 'Baetica revolted' 579-584 and says orthodox bishops supported him.

region.text: Baetica, whose rebellion under Hermenegild the Liuvigild page dates 579-584

ledger.note: 584: Seville falls to a siege and the revolt is over. 'Hermenegild fled to Seville and when it fell to a siege in 584, he went to Cordoba'; he was executed on 13 April 585.

wars.name: Revolt of Hermenegild

zones.text: Baetica, whose rebellion under Hermenegild the Liuvigild page dates 579-584

wars.outcome: Liuvigild takes Merida (582) and Seville (584); Hermenegild is imprisoned and executed on 13 April 585.

certainty.note: The pages name Seville, Cordoba and Baetica but no frontier.

sources.title: Hermenegild
sources.note: Revolt in 580, Seville 584, Byzantine withdrawal, execution 13 April 585.

notes: The rebel's allies are not territory: the Suebi, who had backed him, 'capitulated once again in 583' and the Byzantines withdrew in 584 after Liuvigild paid 30,000 pieces of gold (Hermenegild page). The Hermenegild page says nothing of a royal proclamation or the extent of the kingdom; Cordoba was his refuge in 584.
